# How to Practise a Job Interview Out Loud with ChatGPT's Voice Mode

> **In short:** ChatGPT's Voice Mode lets you have a real spoken conversation — no typing. You can answer interview questions out loud and get immediate, helpful feedback on how your answers land, without the awkward silence of practising alone in a mirror.

Most people who dread job interviews practise the wrong way. They think through answers in their head, or mutter half-sentences while doing the dishes. But an interview is a *spoken* performance — and you need to rehearse it the way it will actually happen. ChatGPT's Voice Mode gives you a patient, judgment-free practice partner you can talk to anytime. Here's how to use it.

## Before you start

- **A ChatGPT account** — the free plan works, though Voice Mode may be slightly faster on Plus ($20/month).
- **The ChatGPT mobile app** — Voice Mode is built into the app on iPhone and Android. It does not work on a desktop browser.
- **Microphone permission** — the app will ask to use your mic the first time you tap it.
- **A quiet moment** — you need to speak out loud, so find a private space.
- **About 15–20 minutes** — enough for two or three full practice runs.

## Step 1 — Open the ChatGPT app and find the voice button

Unlock your phone and tap the **ChatGPT app** icon (a green-and-white chat bubble). If you do not have the app yet, open your phone's app store, search for "ChatGPT," and download it for free before continuing.

Once the app opens, you will see the main chat screen. At the bottom of the screen there is a **text input bar** with a keyboard icon on the left and a send arrow on the right. Just above that bar, in the bottom-right corner, look for a **small headphones or sound-wave icon** 🎧 — that is the Voice Mode button. Tap it once.

A pulsing circle appears on screen and the keyboard slides down out of the way. The app is now listening.

💬 Example: *Tap the headphones icon and wait for the pulsing listening circle.*
You'll know it worked when the keyboard disappears and a round animated circle replaces it, indicating the app is ready to hear your voice.

## Step 2 — Ask ChatGPT to be your interview coach

With the listening circle on screen, speak your opening request clearly. Do not worry about phrasing it perfectly — just say what you want. For example, ask ChatGPT to pretend to be a hiring manager. Keep your request brief so the app hears it clearly.

If Voice Mode does not respond to your first sentence, make sure you are speaking loudly enough and that no other audio is playing. Some phones need a moment to switch the microphone over. If you still see only the listening circle, tap it once to cancel and try again.

💬 Example: *"Please act as a hiring manager and ask me common interview questions."*
You'll know it worked when ChatGPT responds verbally — you hear a voice reply and a transcript of what it said appears in the chat window.

## Step 3 — Answer each question out loud

ChatGPT will now ask you a question — something typical like "Tell me about yourself" or "What is your greatest strength?" When you hear the question, take a breath, and answer it the way you would in a real interview. Speak at a natural pace, make eye contact with your phone as if it were a person across a desk, and aim for two to three minutes per answer.

Do not worry if you stumble or lose your train of thought. That is the whole point of practising. The app will not judge you, interrupt you, or look impatient. If you go quiet for a moment, it will wait — or gently prompt you to continue.

If ChatGPT does not seem to hear a word correctly, try rephrasing it. Some background noise can cause the voice recognizer to miss small words. Rephrasing usually fixes it.

💬 Example: *If it asks, "What is your greatest strength?", say: "I would say my greatest strength is my ability to manage competing deadlines. In my previous role I regularly had three or four projects running at once, and I learned to prioritize by impact rather than urgency."*
You'll know it worked when you see your spoken words appear as text in the chat and ChatGPT moves on to ask a follow-up question.

## Step 4 — Listen to its feedback after each answer

After you finish an answer, ChatGPT will often give you brief feedback right away — maybe praise for a specific point, or a gentle suggestion. Listen to what it says. It might flag that you went on too long, that you did not give a concrete example, or that your answer felt vague.

This is the most valuable part of the practice. You get to hear how your answer actually *sounds* to someone hearing it for the first time, and you get specific, actionable notes. Do not be surprised if the feedback feels blunt — ChatGPT is trying to be genuinely helpful, not harsh.

If you disagree with a piece of feedback, that is fine. You can say so and explain your reasoning. Interview coaching is not about getting one "right" answer — it is about finding your own authentic voice. But do listen carefully and consider each point.

💬 Example: *After your answer about managing deadlines, ChatGPT might say: "Good — you named a specific skill and gave a real example. Try also mentioning one tool you used, like a project management app, to make it even more concrete."*
You'll know it worked when you hear specific, constructive feedback that tells you something useful about your answer.

## Step 5 — Ask for harder or different questions

Once you have done two or three standard questions, guide the conversation. Ask ChatGPT to give you behavioural questions — the kind that start with "Tell me about a time when…" These are the questions people find hardest because they require you to tell a real story from your past.

If you are applying for a specific role or industry, ask it to tailor the questions. ChatGPT can switch into "marketing manager interview" or "customer service interview" mode and ask industry-relevant questions you might actually face.

💬 Example: *"Can you ask me a behavioural question about dealing with a difficult customer?"*
You'll know it worked when the next question starts with something like "Tell me about a time when…" and you feel a slight pressure to recall a real experience from your own past.

## Step 6 — Do a final mock run without stopping

After two or three practice rounds, ask ChatGPT for a complete mock interview. Tell it to ask you six questions in a row without giving feedback until the end — this simulates the real experience of an interview where the interviewer does not pause to coach you. Answer each one, keep going even if you stumble, and resist the urge to restart an answer.

At the end, ask ChatGPT to review the whole performance. This gives you the big-picture view: What was clear? What needed more detail? What felt stiff or rehearsed? This kind of holistic review is harder to get from friends or family who might be too nice to give honest criticism.

💬 Example: *"Run me through a full mock interview with six questions, then give me overall feedback at the end."*
You'll know it worked when you complete six questions back-to-back and receive a summary of your strengths and areas to improve.

## Common mistakes

- **Answering in your head rather than out loud.** Voice Mode only helps if you actually speak. Thinking through an answer silently does not train your speaking voice, your pace, or your confidence. Force yourself to say every word out loud, even if it feels silly at first.

- **Reading from notes while you speak.** This is tempting, but it trains the wrong skill. In most real interviews you will not have notes in front of you. Practise without them, even if your answer is imperfect. The goal is to build the habit of speaking clearly without a script.

- **Ignoring the feedback because it feels harsh.** ChatGPT is not trying to upset you — it is flagging things a real interviewer might also notice. If something feels uncomfortable to hear, that is often exactly the thing worth working on. Sit with the feedback for a moment before moving on.

## What this means for you

- **In everyday life:** You can practise for any high-stakes conversation — a salary negotiation, a presentation at work, or a difficult conversation with a colleague — using the same method. Voice Mode is a free, private rehearsal space available any time you have your phone.

- **For your business or work:** If you are hiring or managing others, use Voice Mode to prepare for candidate interviews yourself. Understanding what a strong answer sounds like helps you recognise good candidates when you meet them.

- **If you're just getting started:** Your very first move is the simplest: open the app, tap the headphones icon, and say one sentence about yourself. Just one. That is enough to get comfortable with the experience before you tackle full interview answers.

## Try it now

Open ChatGPT on your phone right now, tap the voice button, and say: *"I am practising for a job interview. Can you ask me a question?"* Do not overthink it — just do it. You will be five minutes into your first practice before you have time to talk yourself out of it.
